newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals rose 34.7 percent in January over the same period last year, the finance ministry said on Monday.
The ministry collected $10.98 million compared with $8.15 in January 1996, it said in a statement.
Collected revenues for 1996 totalled $180.58 million, 31 percent up from $137.74 million collected in 1995, according to figures issued by the ministry last week.

Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district, but average about 6.5 percent. However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts said.
The dollar figures are based on the following exchange rates:
$1=1,592 Lebanese pounds at end of January 1997
